title: Writing a work instruction
body:
You are authoring this T (work-instruction) directly instead of the server
emitting a fixed template. Reflect the actual context of this group and the findings
of the preceding investigation. A good T DIRECTS the work the paired TR will carry
out. Cover:
- Purpose/scope: what change is being made and why (tie it to the driving R/B + NR).
- Work items: the concrete, ordered work items (files/areas to touch, the approach).
- Completion criteria: how the TR proves it is done (tests to run GREEN, acceptance checks).
Keep it an instruction: direct the work; the implementation + evidence belong in the
TR that follows. Do NOT implement the code in this step — write the directive.

When the mention has an 'Instruction to include next document header' section, include the
next-document header exactly as given there (next_type / project / module / group / title / target_id).
When the mention asks you to write into an existing document (edit), it has no such section: keep
that document's existing header (front matter) as it is and add no next-document header.
On submit this instruction is auto-approved (non-{M,CH}) like any managed instruction and
the unmanned chain proceeds to its paired report step.
